sentences.text: 1. Heard learned counsels for the parties and perused the record.

2. The present petition is directed against the order dated 24.02.2025 passed by the Reference Court under Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956, deciding the dispute pertaining to apportionment of compensation with respect to the acquired land.

3. The petitioner herein is claiming right in the property in question, which was subject matter of acquisition on the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/3851/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/05/2025 undefined basis of an agreement to sell dated 24.08.1994.

It is sought to be stated in the present petition that on receipt of the sale consideration, the physical possession of the land in question was handed over to the petitioner who is in peaceful and vacant possession of the subject land and cultivating the same.
The petitioner claims possessary title over the subject land.
It is further stated that as the vendor had refused to execute the sale deed, the petitioner filed a civil suit, viz.
Regular
Civil Suit No. 668 of 1995
seeking permanent injunction in relation to the subject land against the vendors/original owners

. During the pendency of the suit, an interim injunction application was filed which was allowed by the competent court on 29.01.1996 directing the parties to maintain status quo with respect to the subject land as per the report of the Court Commissioner.
The further contention in the petition is that on 07.08.2006, the suit was dismissed for default, but on the same day it was restored.
The trial court has further framed issues and decreed the suit on 30.03.2007 for permanent injunction.
The mutation entry no. 1642 dated 17.07.2008 had been posted recording the decree, which was duly certified.
4. Further, on 07.09.1995, civil suit viz. Special Civil Suit No. 381 of 1995 has been filed by the petitioner seeking a decree of specific performance of agreement to sell dated 24.08.1994 and
the said suit is pending as on date.

It is further contended that during the pendency of the suit for permanent injunction and specific performance NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/3851/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/05/2025 undefined of agreement to sell, the original owners, in clear defiance of the order of injunction dated 30.03.2007 passed by the Civil Court in Regular Civil Suit No. 668 of 1995 had conveyed the land in question vide registered sale deed no. 4952 dated 07.05.2004 in favour of respondent no.3 herein.

It is then contended that on the strength of the sale deed, the respondent no.3 had instituted a civil suit, viz. Regular Civil Suit No. 230 of 2010 against the original owner/vendor and the present petitioner seeking decree of declaration and permanent injunction for the relief that the injunction decree dated 30.03.2007 was not binding on him, but the said suit was unconditionally withdrawn by the respondent no.3 vide withdrawal purshis and the order dated 01.12.2023 had been passed therein.

5. The petitioner herein further filed civil suit being Regular Civil Suit No. 207 of 2016 against the respondent no.3 challenging the sale deed dated 07.05.2004 wherein the original owners/vendors were also impleaded.
It is an admission on the part of the petitioner that the said suit has been dismissed under Order VII Rule 11 (d) filed by the respondent no.3 herein.

6. The petitioner then impleaded the respondent no.3 as party defendant in the civil suit filed for specific performance of agreement, viz. Special Civil Suit No. 381 of 1995, which is pending as on date.

The order of impleadment of the respondent no.3 in the said suit, NEUTRAL CITATION Karshanbhai Kalidas Panchal vs Competent Authority (National Highway ... on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193621934/
2 C/SCA/3851/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/05/2025 undefined however was challenged before this Court in Special Civil Application No. 780 of 2020, which has been allowed and the impleadment order has been set aside on account of dismissal of Special Civil Suit No. 207 of 2016 where the petitioner has challenged the validity of the sale deed executed in favour of the respondent no.3.
7.

sentences.text: Mr. N.V. Gandhi, learned advocate for the petitioner vehemently argued that in the order passed by the Reference court, it has wrongly been noted that the original owner had sold the land in question after dismissal of the Regular Civil Suit No. 668 of 1995 for default.

The contention is that the sale deed in favour of the respondent no.3 was executed on 07.05.2004 in utter violation of the interim injunction order dated 29.01.1996 passed in Regular Civil Suit No. 668 of 1995.
The sale deed, therefore, is liable to be declared as void ab initio.

8. Insofar as the dismissal of the Regular Civil Suit No. 668 of 1995, by placing the entry made on the plaint at page 60 of the paper book, it was sought to be submitted that the said suit was dismissed for default on 07.08.2006 and was restored on the said date itself.
9. Be that as it may, the fact remains that the respondent no.3 is in possession of a registered sale deed dated 07.05.2004, which has not been declared invalid or canceled by any court of law.

The suit filed by the petitioner in the year 2016 for cancellation of the sale deed has been dismissed under Order VII Rule 11 CPC, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/3851/2025 ORDER DATED:
05/05/2025 undefined which order has attained finality.

It is further relevant to note that the petitioner is claiming right in the property on the basis of an agreement to sell dated 24.08.1994,
with respect to which, the suit for specific performance of agreement against the original owner, i.e.
Special Civil Suit No. 381 of 1995 is pending.
10.
As on date, the petitioner has no right to claim the possession of the property in question.
The contention in the petition that the petitioner has possessary title over the subject land need not be gone into inasmuch as, the suit for specific performance of agreement to sell is pending.

We need not go into the merits of the claim of the petitioner seeking specific performance of agreement to sell dated 24.08.1994, but the fact remains that the petitioner cannot claim disbursement of compensation on the ground of pendency of the civil suit seeking for specific performance of agreement to sell or the sale deed dated 07.05.2004 in favour of the respondent no.3 being in violation of the interim injunction order.

Moreover, the decree for permanent injunction dated 30.03.2007 was granted when the sale deed was already executed without bringing the purchaser,
namely the respondent no.3, on record.
11.

For the above noted facts, we do not find any error in the decision of the Reference court in allowing the reference and declaring the respondent no.3/opponent no.2 therein being entitled to the compensation amount in the reference along with the interest accrued thereto.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/3851/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/05/2025 undefined

As regards the claim of the petitioner herein, it is observed by the Reference court that if any competent Civil court passes decree against the respondent no.3/opponent no.2, the compensation amount is to be repaid in future.

sentences.text:
For any dispute pertaining to the right of the petitioner to seek compensation account, in our considered opinion the dispute can only be adjudicated by the civil court where the petitioner is seeking relief of title to the property, which had been sold in favour of respondent no.3 vide registered sale deed dated 07.05.2004.
13.
For the above, the present petition is found devoid of merits and hence, dismissed.
